chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Ghazwan, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: When the people of Lut did what they did, the earth cried out to its Lord until its tears reached the sky, and the sky cried out until its tears reached the Throne. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to the sky: 'Rain stones upon them,' and He revealed to the earth: 'Swallow them.'
ai.seo_question: What was the specific divine punishment for the people of Lut as described in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the cosmic scale of divine retribution by personifying the earth and sky as weeping witnesses to the sins of Lot’s people. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interconnectedness of creation in responding to moral transgression, where natural elements actively participate in executing Allah’s command. The text serves as a vivid illustration of how physical punishment is preceded by spiritual and cosmic signs of displeasure.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  relates  that  the  community  of Prophet  Lut  (a.s.)  was  involved  in  homosexual  relations excessively. Hence, the earth cried so much in front of the Lord that its tears reached the heavens and heavens cried so much that their tears reached the Divine Throne. Then Allah ordered  the  sky  to  rain  stones  on  those  people  and  He ordered the earth to swallow them.”
